title: Past-Due Grace and Suspension Days by Paloma Business Plan
content:
When a Paloma Business account becomes past due, two plan figures run in calendar days from that point: the grace days during which payouts may still be submitted, and the days after which the account is suspended if still unpaid.

| | Paloma Business Starter | Paloma Business Essentials | Paloma Business Growth | Paloma Business Pro | Paloma Business Scale | Paloma Business Enterprise |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Past-due grace (calendar days during which payouts may still be submitted) | 7 | 7 | 10 | 14 | 14 | 30 |
| Suspension point (calendar days after becoming past due, if still unpaid) | 14 | 14 | 21 | 30 | 30 | 45 |

### Dated illustration (hypothetical dates)

| Plan | Became past due | Last day of payout grace | Suspension point if still unpaid |
|---|---|---|---|
| Paloma Business Essentials | 1 March | 8 March | 15 March |
| Paloma Business Growth | 1 March | 11 March | 22 March |
| Paloma Business Enterprise | 1 March | 31 March | 15 April |

On every plan the grace figure is shorter than the suspension figure.
